_comment: Source of truth for framework and plugin migration versions. Written by install_plugin.sh (plugin section) and updated manually by framework developers (framework section). Never hardcode this data in version.py.

framework_migrations.description: Initial schema — users, guilds, permissions, audit log, LLM tracking, app config
Guild isolation — PostgreSQL Row-Level Security on all guild-scoped tables
Migration history — audit trail of every schema upgrade (who, when, duration, result)
Instrumentation — card_usage, guild_events, request_metrics, bot_command_metrics tables; app_config table for dynamic runtime configuration
Fix RLS policies — guard NULLIF empty-string cast to bigint, bypass check first
Public site surface — globally-unique guild slug for Level 0 per-server public sites (configurable /p prefix)
Harden guild RLS — allow guild_id IS NULL inserts on llm_usage/llm_usage_summary (system/global LLM cost rows) and degrade an empty-string guild context to NULL instead of erroring

Editable LLM Configs storage — llm_schemas + llm_function_sets (global tables backing the dashboard structured-output schema + function-calling set editors). Ported from baseline; re-id'd from c1d2e3f4a5b6 to e5f6a7b8c9d0 to avoid colliding with the ai_player plugin migration, still on the independent framework branch.

LLM cost tracking — composite UNIQUE(provider, model) on llm_model_pricing, seed default per-1k pricing (incl. per-provider default), and backfill cost on zero-cost historical llm_usage rows. Ported from baseline a8b9c0d1e2f3; down_revision re-pointed from c1d2e3f4a5b6 (= ai_player here) to the framework 1.7.0 head e5f6a7b8c9d0.

plugin_migrations.description: Rama única de la app del Mundial (el framework permanece independiente): worldcup_data (datos: equipos, grupos, partidos, bracket), predictions (quiniela con RLS por servidor) y ai_player (jugador IA: análisis por partido con grounding y decisión almacenada). Todas las migraciones de la app van en esta rama, en orden: worldcup_data → predictions → ai_player.

Ingests goal video clips from the Fox browser extension, stores them on the shared data volume, and exposes a public serving endpoint. The live_tracker cog pairs each clip with a stream-confirmed goal and posts it instead of a gif.
